tb21_profile.skill: Clone and build a large legacy C++ ML framework CPU-only, survive its dependency and compiler problems, then drive its CLI to train a CNN to a stated accuracy floor and read the metrics back out of the log
tb21_profile.domain: Caffe 1.0.0 / C++ deep-learning framework build (make or cmake, protobuf, boost, CPU_ONLY), CIFAR-10, solver prototxt, CNN training metrics
tb21_profile.task_form: build-from-source plus run-a-training-job-to-a-metric-threshold; multi-stage pipeline verified on the produced model file and accuracy numbers

verifier_notes: machine-learning_20260604_144210_001 (Darknet) is graded weak (2/14 substantive) yet it is the single closest domain analogue to Caffe — original C vision framework, Makefile feature flags, download weights, run the CLI. I kept it in per_source and in final rank 9 on skill, but downstream should know its suite is mostly exists/substring checks. TerminalWorld's ML-plus-build offerings are mostly FREE: tw_423671 (Gunrock CUDA build, the best build analogue there) and tw_588262 (YOLOv4 compiled from source) are both FREE and are listed in per_source only, as the spec allows. Terminal-Lego's DL cluster is a wall of 'demonstrate/explain Keras' scripts; its one genuinely Caffe-specific task, task_13577, is honestly strong (15 of 21 tests pin computed learning-rate values).
searches: tools.py search tmax 'accuracy of at least|accuracy (must|should) (be|exceed)|at least [0-9]{2}% accuracy|test accuracy' -n 25
tools.py words tmax train accuracy compile source epochs -n 25
tools.py search smith 'learning rate|optimizer|gradient|epoch|batch norm|convolution|image classif' -n 20

CalibForge.reason: CPU-only source tree that fails to compile: fix it, install, then train with fixed hyperparameters and clear 80% test accuracy. Structurally identical.
Build XGBoost 1.7.0 CPU-only in /app/xgboost, then train and clear a stated ROC-AUC floor. Same build-then-train-to-a-threshold pipeline.
Build the CRFsuite C++ library from source and train a model on supplied train/test files; strongest verifier of the build-and-train family.
fastText 0.9.2 refuses to compile on this system; fix the C++ build, then train a text classifier. The compile-errors half of Caffe exactly.
mlpack 4.5.1 CPU-only via cmake with none of its dependencies installed, then build a program against it. Dependency hell like Caffe's.
Set up Tencent ncnn from source and run SqueezeNet CNN classification over an image directory. Same C++ CNN framework territory.
Build XGBoost 1.7.6 CPU-only from source then train a binary classifier with it; pinned-value tests on the trained result.
Faiss 1.7.4 CPU-only with AVX2, shared library plus Python bindings — the configure-the-build-variant skill Caffe's CPU_ONLY needs.
Clone pjreddie/darknet, build with OpenCV, fetch weights, run detection and parse results. Closest living relative of the Caffe task.
Clone XGBoost 1.7.0 to /app/xgboost, build, train a regression model; every test pins a computed value.

TMax-15K.reason: Iterate on a data-prep script until an external evaluator reports ACCURACY at least 0.85 — the same train-until-the-metric-clears loop, fully pinned tests.
Fix a leaky evaluation then tune the pipeline until honest test accuracy reaches 0.75 and save the fitted model. Threshold-driven training.
Train and serialise a model that must score at least 0.80 on a fresh holdout drawn from the same generator. Same accept-on-accuracy shape.
Suspiciously high test accuracy from a KNN pipeline; find the leakage and get honest numbers. Teaches reading train-vs-test gaps, which this task checks.
Repair a script that joins data, trains a neural network and benchmarks inference; multi-stage training pipeline with several planted faults.
Install PyTorch into the environment, rebuild a network from a stored weight description and run inference. Every test pins a value.
Air-gapped vendored package will not build; patch its C sources until install succeeds. Covers the compile half, not the training half.
Build a model judged on a hidden test set at 0.85 accuracy, plus produce a cross-validation artefact. Same reward-on-metric structure.
Create the Python environment, clean data, then train a baseline classifier end to end; environment setup plus training in one task.
Fixed-seed PCA plus classifier with test accuracy recorded for experiment tracking; small, and no build or framework work at all.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Implement Caffe's lr_policy schedules from the solver prototxt semantics; literally the configuration file cifar10_quick_solver.prototxt uses.
A DL framework refuses to run because a shared library is missing; locate and wire up the right library. Caffe's link-time pain, weakly tested.
Diagnose why the framework does not see the accelerator and get the runtime consistent. Same environment-vs-framework debugging.
Implement forward and backward passes by hand; teaches what a solver iteration actually does, which the accuracy check depends on.
TensorFlow fails to load its dynamic libraries; resolve the loader paths. Exactly the class of failure a from-source Caffe hits.
Fix a neural network that will not learn on a binary task so it reaches usable accuracy; the training-actually-converges half.
Loss goes NaN during training; find the causes and stabilise it. Diagnosing a training run from its log, as here.
Accuracy stagnates in a Keras classifier; identify why and get it moving. Same symptom as a Caffe run that never reaches 45%.
Fix NaN/Inf values in a CNN training script on RGB images; right subject area, but a small scripted fix and thin tests.
Add L1/L2 regularisation in PyTorch without manual loops; framework API knowledge only, no build and no training target.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Split a dataset, drive the LIBSVM CLI to train a model file and report validation accuracy. Same train-via-a-C++-tool-and-check-accuracy loop.
Same LIBSVM train-and-validate workflow with a weaker verifier; the model file and accuracy are the deliverables.
Clone with submodules and build a CUDA project under an old GCC toolchain — the closest analogue to Caffe's build, but graded FREE.
Compile OpenCV bindings from source with precompiled artefacts disabled and run YOLOv4 inference; right work, FREE verifier.
Clone, check out a branch and autotools-build a large C project, then install it. The build half, verified.
Build an image-processing benchmark out-of-tree against GraphicsMagick and run it; compile plus execute plus collect results.
Define a PyTorch CNN and profile it into two output files; model definition and metric extraction, no build.
Compile an old academic C toolkit from its repo and install its evaluation binary; hand-written makefiles like Caffe's.
Long configure-and-compile of a kernel tree; shares only the endurance and configuration part of a big from-source build.
Train a compass model and two slice models with a library CLI and compute a score; training via tooling, tiny scale.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Instantiate a PyTorch architecture from a JSON model definition — the same read-a-config-file-into-a-network step as the solver and net prototxt.
Create the venv, install the library, download the MNIST data files and run the classification workflow. Mirrors get_cifar10 plus train.
Clone an image-classification repo into a fixed path, set it up and run its example end to end; same clone-configure-run chain.
Run the repo's own MNIST digit-classification workflow after provisioning its environment and datasets.
Run a provided workflow that trains a scikit-learn classifier and emits predictions; training pipeline, no build.
Assemble and execute an ML pipeline that loads data, selects features and trains a classifier to produce predictions.
Compile a C++ toolkit from its repository and install its binary; supplies the build half RTS's ML tasks lack.
Install every build dependency yourself then autotools-build a cloned C project — the dependency-resolution work Caffe demands.
Train a compass model and two slice models with the CADE library and compute a shift score; training by CLI, trivial scale.
Download a large source tarball and build and install it under a prefix; only the build half, unrelated subject.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Milestone-based parameter scheduler computes the wrong step points — the same learning-rate-schedule reasoning as the solver's lr_policy.
Batch-norm running mean and variance stop updating; understanding train-time BN statistics is central to getting a CNN to its accuracy target.
PeriodicCheckpointer misbehaves — the snapshot-every-N-iterations machinery that produces cifar10_quick_iter_N.caffemodel.
CNN block built with the wrong activation and an inverted 3d flag; reading a network definition against its intended architecture.
smooth_l1_loss breaks for tiny beta; loss-function numerics of the kind that silently stall training.
Weight initialisation crashes when a layer has no bias; layer-initialisation semantics that Caffe's filler configuration also encodes.
Checkpoint load/save ordering bug in a vision training library; model-persistence debugging, same lineage as Caffe.
Parameter counts do not aggregate over submodules; requires walking a network graph, but no training involved.
Einsum FLOP accounting is wrong; analysis tooling around CNNs rather than training them.
Model summary printing is malformed; same library and model-graph objects, but the fix is formatting.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Loss tracker breaks across repeated compiles when driving train_on_batch; debugging a training loop's metric bookkeeping.
Saving a subclassed model to a checkpoint file fails; the model-snapshot serialisation this task's .caffemodel check depends on.
Deep-learning library failing in a specific CUDA/GCC environment; getting a framework to work on the machine you have.
Preprocessing layer misbehaves when a saved model is reloaded; data-pipeline plus serialisation in a training framework.
Implement tensor operations to match PyTorch's in-place semantics exactly; framework-internals work, no build or training run.
Batch evaluation silently returns wrongly shaped outputs; the silent-wrong-numbers failure mode of a model pipeline.
Classification pipeline explanation bug in an AutoML library; shares the train-a-classifier vocabulary and little else.
Seeding and reproducibility of training runs; relevant to hitting a deterministic accuracy bar, but the fix is API design.
Framework-internal Keras defect; same deep-learning ecosystem, no transfer to building or driving a trainer.
Advanced-indexing semantics diverge from numpy and torch; array-library correctness, thin transfer to this task.

final_top10.reason: CPU-only source build that fails to compile, fix it, install, train with fixed hyperparameters, clear 80% accuracy. Same two-stage task.
Build XGBoost 1.7.0 CPU-only into /app/xgboost then train until a stated metric floor is cleared. Same build-then-train contract.
Build a C++ sequence-labelling library from source and train a model on the supplied data; best-verified member of this family.
fastText 0.9.2 will not compile here; repair the C++ build, then train a classifier with the binary you produced.
Clone pjreddie/darknet, build with OpenCV support, fetch weights and run the CLI over images. Nearest thing to Caffe in the pool.
Set up ncnn from source and classify images with SqueezeNet; C++ CNN framework built by hand, then driven for inference.
cmake CPU-only build of mlpack with no dependencies pre-installed, then a program compiled against it. Caffe's dependency problem.
Another CPU-only XGBoost source build followed by training a classifier; pinned-value tests on the trained output.
Faiss CPU-only with AVX2, shared library and bindings — practising exactly the build-variant flags Caffe's CPU_ONLY switch controls.
Split the data, run the LIBSVM trainer CLI to produce a model file and report validation accuracy. The train-and-measure half, strongly verified.

notes: CalibForge owns this task: it contains a dense family of 'build <C/C++ ML library> from source (often CPU-only, often with deliberate compile errors) and then train a model to a metric threshold' tasks, which is caffe-cifar-10's exact two-stage structure, with strong verifiers on most of them. Nine of the final ten are CalibForge; the tenth is TerminalWorld's LIBSVM task, chosen over further XGBoost near-duplicates for variety in the training-CLI half. Terminal-Lego beats the old pool in one narrow place only: task_13577 is Caffe-specific (solver lr_policy) and genuinely strong, which nothing in the v1 pool offers — but the rest of its ML block is 'write a script that demonstrates X in Keras', which does not transfer. TerminalWorld's best build analogues (tw_423671 Gunrock/CUDA, tw_588262 YOLOv4) are FREE and therefore per_source only. Recursive-Task-Synthesis offers essentially one task duplicated dozens of times (sds-mnist clone/venv/download/run); ranks 2-4 there are near-identical variants and merge should treat them as one item. SWE-Smith reduces entirely to fvcore, which is the right lineage (Detectron/Caffe2 vision utilities) but bug-fix shaped.
